title: Beat & Motion
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Tatsuhiko gave up his childhood dream of animation after being teased, then lost his music too when his band broke up, and became cynical about all dreams. A drunk stranger yells at him for mocking a friend's dream, and he starts animating again; his idol, independent musician Nico, then asks him to make her music video, and she turns out to be that stranger. The two encourage each other while facing record-label setbacks and old friendships (Wikipedia; Viz blurb via AniList and MU).
life_message: Dreams are worth pursuing even after failure, and people who believe in each other can restart their creative lives.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are emotional, e.g. Miyu demanding answers from Nico (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Leaving set paths to chase art (Viz blurb; Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friends and collaborators, not family, are the support (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Fan and idol become equal partners (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern media careers; no religion or custom (MU).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Self-expression over a stable job is the core theme (Viz; Wikipedia).

folkways.japan: Teasing that crushes a child's dream and the weight of a steady corporate path reflect Japanese conformity pressures the story pushes against.

delivery.evidence: The turning point is Nico yelling at Tatsuhiko about dreams (Wikipedia); reviewer calls it 'hard-hitting' (Multiversity, via Wikipedia).
delivery.note: The cynical view belongs to the hero himself and is treated with sympathy before he outgrows it.

winners_losers: Tatsuhiko and Nico both gain from believing in each other; cynicism loses. Sympathy goes to dream-chasers.
